## Design roles

Each part does a job for the person. These are the jobs, as questions the part answers.

<div class="odv-am-rolelist"><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Containment</b> What holds this?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Layering</b> What sits on top?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Hierarchy</b> What do you read first?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Readability</b> Can you read it?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Emphasis</b> Where does the eye go?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Meaning</b> What state is it in?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Affordance</b> Can you act on it?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Feedback</b> Did it respond?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Focus</b> Where is the keyboard?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Grouping</b> What belongs together?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Reach</b> Can you hit it?</span></div>

## How the decisions reach each part

Each part follows a chain: an answer about the product, the rule it set, the token that carries it, and the value you see. The numbers match the drawing.

<section class="odv-am-card" id="part-1-2-3"><div class="odv-am-img wide"><span class="odv-am-assetbox odv-am-pending">Drawn in Figma by the Open DS anatomy plugin; the image is not exported yet.</span></div><div class="odv-am-body"><header><i class="odv-am-n">1</i><i class="odv-am-n">2</i><i class="odv-am-n">3</i><b>Surface, border and shadow</b><span class="odv-am-role" title="What holds this?">Containment</span><span class="odv-am-role" title="What sits on top?">Layering</span></header><ul class="odv-am-tree"><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Answer</b><div class="odv-am-main">Elevation · What rises above the page? → Only what floats</div><div class="odv-am-why">Only menus and dialogs float; cards use lines.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Answer</b><div class="odv-am-main">Elevation · What separates groups on the page? → Lines</div><div class="odv-am-why">Thin lines guide the eye along rows.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Answer</b><div class="odv-am-main">Shape · What should control corners say? → Slightly rounded</div><div class="odv-am-why">Small corners keep dense rows straight.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Rule</b><div class="odv-am-main">For a card on the page, use A hairline border, no shadow. Don't use a shadow.</div><div class="odv-am-why">On a busy grid, lines separate. ## For agents

Agents get this same anatomy: every part, its roles, whether it is required, the tokens it reads and the decisions behind them.

- **From an AI agent:** call the `get_anatomy` tool on the Open DS MCP server, with this scheme and `card`.
- **From a terminal:** `npx open-ds anatomy dense-data card`
